editorial:
Chun-Li grows up watching her father taken by crime boss M. Bison, then trains to fight back. Years later, she leaves her old life behind and heads into a dangerous world of crime, secret fighters, and revenge. The movie tries to mix martial arts action with a serious origin story, but it often feels flat and rushed. Kristin Kreuk looks the part, yet the story gives her little room to shine. Neal McDonough plays Bison as a cold villain, while Chris Klein’s cop subplot feels out of place. You get a few flashy fights and city scenes, but the energy rarely lasts.

If you are a die-hard Street Fighter fan, you may still want to see how they handle Chun-Li’s backstory. Everyone else will likely find the pacing uneven, the dialogue stiff, and the action less exciting than expected. It is not a total disaster, but it misses the fun spirit of the games. Watch it only if you are curious, maybe as a cheap rental or background movie. For a better night, stream something stronger in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent a sharper action film on Apple TV, or grab a 4K Blu-ray you already trust.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Chun-Li confronts M. Bison after learning the truth about her father and his criminal empire. Their fight ends with Bison defeated, and Chun-Li avenges her father. She also stops Bison’s plan to control the city, while the police close in on his operation. The movie closes with Chun-Li accepting her role as a protector, hinting that her fight is not over. There is no big twist beyond the reveal of Bison’s power and family secrets, but the ending tries to set up more adventures.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves video game movies or wants to see every Street Fighter adaptation.
